title: Fine-grained Telemetry Consent Hooks & Tiered Retention Matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a consent-first telemetry workflow that tags events at ingestion with tenant- and session-level consent, classifies sensitive fields at ingest-time, and enforces a configurable tiered retention matrix. This ticket covers: (1) SDK/agent consent hooks (client-side and service-side), (2) ingestion-time classifier & scrubber, (3) tiered retention enforcement and TTL metadata, and (4) immutable audit entries for access and retention actions. The design favors deterministic pseudonymization for identifiers, time-binned TTLs for different data classes, and a policy engine that evaluates tenant overrides and legal hold flags. Implementation must integrate with existing RBAC/access-logging and the console dashboards for compliance monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Client SDKs expose synchronous consent hooks and a non-blocking async fallback for missing consent metadata.
Ingest pipeline classifies 95% of incoming telemetry into defined data classes (public, internal, sensitive-PII, sensitive-PII-restricted) within 200ms median added latency.
Retention matrix applied: default TTLs enforced per data class; tenant overrides honored with exponential backoff for rollbacks.
Pseudonymization applied to PII fields using tenant-salted, HSM-backed key derivation; no reversible plaintext retained in observability store.
Access events (who, why, query) are emitted to an append-only audit stream with tamper-evident metadata and surfaced in the console within 10 minutes.
End-to-end tests and canary deployed pipeline show <0.5% error rate and no more than 5% traffic increase in ingest latency on median workloads.
Legal and Security sign-off obtained for retention bands and pseudonymization scheme.
Operational runbook and migration notes published to Confluence.
Dashboards updated with telemetry labeling coverage, scrub rates, retention enforcement failures, and audit query volume.
Backfill/migration tool to reclassify historical events supports checkpointing and rate limiting to avoid tenant impact.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Launch SDK consent hooks (opt-out safe default) and ingest-time dry-run classification for 10% of traffic. Phase 2: Enable enforced scrubber for sensitive classes in a canary (1 tenant, low volume). Phase 3: Ramp enforcement to all tenants that have no legal hold and observe metrics for 2 weeks. Phase 4: Run backfill job to reclassify retained historical telemetry for tenants that elected stricter retention; backfill uses tenant-scoped rate limit and writes checkpoint to audit ledger. Each phase gated by security/legal sign-off and automated smoke tests.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged server and SDK changes. 2) Canary to internal Redwood tenants and two pilot customers. 3) Monitor labeling coverage, scrub false positives, and audit-log generation for 72 hours. 4) If metrics stable, progressively enable for 25%, 50%, 100% traffic with one-week observation windows. 5) After global enable, run migration backfill for opt-in tenants.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misclassification leading to over-scrubbing. Mitigation: Dry-run mode + golden set tests + manual override in console for emergency reveals (audited).
Risk: Increased ingest latency. Mitigation: Fast-path classification using header flags and lightweight regex matchers; expensive checks queued asynchronously with eventual enforcement.
Risk: Audit ledger growth and cost. Mitigation: Indexed shard policy and 90-day cold tiering for audit metadata; store proofs to external blob with pointer in ledger.
Risk: Tenant key management complexity. Mitigation: Integrate with KMS/HSM and provide default platform-managed keys while supporting Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise tenants.
Risk: Legal hold requirements preventing deletion. Mitigation: Legal hold flag overrides TTL and creates immutable hold record; deletion requests follow a manual review workflow.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK consent flows and ingest classification rules; integration test cluster that runs labeled traffic through the pipeline and asserts TTL metadata and audit events; canary smoke tests for latency and error budgets; chaos-run to validate failure modes of the pseudonymization KMS path.
implementation_notes:
- Add consent header X-RW-CONSENT with structured flags to SDKs; fallback to session and tenant consent resolution.
- Extend ingest proto to include 'data_class' and 'ttl_seconds' fields.
- Scrubber pipeline stage: deterministic pseudonymizer -> field redaction -> schema validation.
- Policy engine service evaluates tenant overrides, legal hold, and region-specific retention rules.
- Append-only audit ledger implemented with content hashes and sequencing; proofs stored in cold blob storage.
- Minimal schema migration: treat missing 'data_class' as 'internal' and apply conservative TTL until reclassified.
